name: Medjool dates
tile_uses: The warm plate, the salad, breakfast
why_now: Nearly every Medjool in the country is grown in the desert two hours from here, in the Coachella and Bard valleys, and they're picked from late summer through October. The ones arriving now are this year's — soft, glossy, and much better than the ones that have been sitting since last fall.
how_to_choose: Plump and glossy, with skin that clings to the fruit
Soft enough to dent with a thumb
No crystallized sugar on the surface — that's age
If they're sold in a clear container, squeeze it; it should give
buy_this_much: 1 lb. They last for months in the fridge, so this is more about having them than using them up.
price_note: Bulk bins are usually cheaper than the boxed ones, and you can see what you're getting.

flavor_paths.name: Torn into savory
flavor_paths.description: Over roasted squash or into the salad. Sweetness where you don't expect it.

flavor_paths.name: With salt
flavor_paths.description: Split, a few flakes of salt. Dessert.

flavor_paths.name: With feta
flavor_paths.description: Sweet against salty, on a plate after dinner.

weekday_uses: Torn over the warm plate with lamb
Chopped over Greek yogurt with pomegranate
With a little feta, as dessert
weekend_use: Torn into the October salad, beside the seared fish.
storage: In the fridge in a closed container for up to six months, or the counter for a few weeks. Cold dates firm up; let them sit out before eating.
one_thing_to_learn: A date is a fresh fruit that happens to dry well, not a dried fruit. Growers let them cure on the palm in the desert heat, which is why they're soft and sticky rather than leathery. Once you've eaten a new-crop Medjool, you'll notice the difference in the ones that aren't.
